name: Spare Room
tagline: Rent out a room in your home, calmly and fairly
about: Spare Room helps homeowners and tenants let a room to a lodger or flatmate: pricing it right, writing the ad, screening applicants, setting house rules and an agreement, and handling problems without falling out.
persona: You are a practical live-in landlord coach: fair to both sides, allergic to vague arrangements, and clear that a written agreement protects the friendship.

onboarding.title: A good lodger starts with a clear deal
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about your home so pricing and rules fit.
bullets: Ads and screening that find good people

tools.title: Price the room
tools.subtitle: Rent, deposit, bills

inputs.label: The room
inputs.placeholder: double, 12 m², built-in wardrobe, no ensuite

tools.prompt: Price this room: {room}. Local evidence: {local}. Bills: {bills}. Produce a kv (suggested rent, range, deposit, what bills add per month, bills-included price), a table (Feature | Adds or subtracts | Amount), bullets on tax-free allowances and declaration rules to check for the region in general terms, and a callout on pricing for the right person rather than the top price.

tools.title: Write the ad
tools.subtitle: A listing that attracts the right person

inputs.label: About the home and you
inputs.placeholder: quiet, work from home, one cat, near the tram, no couples

tools.prompt: Write a room ad aimed at a '{ideal}' lodger for the profile's home: {about}. Produce a quote with a headline and a 120-word listing, bullets of 8 facts the listing must state (rent, bills, deposit, notice, rules), a kv (photo checklist: 5 shots → what each shows), and a callout on discrimination rules and wording to avoid in general terms.

tools.title: Screen applicants
tools.subtitle: Who to shortlist and what to verify

inputs.label: Messages or details
inputs.placeholder: A: nurse, shifts, has references; B: student, parents guarantee; C: vague, wants to move tomorrow

tools.prompt: Screen these applicants for the profile's home: {applicants}. Produce a table (Applicant | Fit | Risk signs | Verify), a checklist of 10 questions for the viewing or call, a quote with a polite decline message and a shortlist message, and a callout on references, ID and right-to-rent style checks that may apply in the region.

tools.title: House rules & agreement
tools.subtitle: Clauses and friendly wording

inputs.label: Your must-haves
inputs.placeholder: no overnight guests midweek, no smoking, kitchen clean by 10pm

tools.prompt: Notice {notice}; must-haves: {dealbreakers}. Produce a checklist of clauses for a lodger agreement (rent, deposit, notice, bills, rooms shared, guests, cleaning, keys, ending it), a kv (each house rule → a friendly one-line wording), bullets on what the profile's status means for permissions and insurance in general terms, and a callout on keeping the agreement in writing and signed by both.

tools.title: Handle a problem
tools.subtitle: Late rent, mess, guests, moving out

inputs.label: What's happening
inputs.placeholder: rent 9 days late, said Friday twice

tools.prompt: Issue: {issue}. Details: {detail}. Produce a quote with a calm message to the lodger, steps for escalation over the next 2–4 weeks, bullets on what a live-in landlord can and cannot do in general terms, and a callout on when to seek local advice or use the deposit.

disclaimer: General information, not legal advice; property law, tenancy rules and taxes vary by country and region — check with a qualified local professional before relying on it.
